title: Rate-Type Eligibility Predicate
purpose: Introduce RATE_TYPE_ELIGIBLE(x, phi) as the first governed admissibility predicate for metric-bridge evaluation while keeping promotion, theorem status, and RT_core unchanged.
summary: This patch registers a governed predicate that screens rate-typed metric-bridge evaluation before any bridge testing is admitted. Passing the screen only admits the candidate to bridge testing; it does not promote any bridge claim or modify RT_core.

basis.scope: Provisional governance-predicate witness that extends the metric-bridge induction path into an explicit admissibility screen while leaving RT_core unchanged and keeping bridge testing deferred.

core_rule.statement: RATE_TYPE_ELIGIBLE(x, phi) may be introduced only as a governance screen for rate-typed metric-bridge evaluation, and passing the screen admits bridge testing only after the declared reference, coupled A|E relation, ordered intermediate relation, endpoint compatibility, and generative exclusion conditions are all recorded.

RateTypeEligibilityPredicate.definition: A governed admissibility predicate stating that system x is eligible for rate-typed metric-bridge evaluation only relative to declared reference phi.
RateTypeEligibilityPredicate.canonical_form: RATE_TYPE_ELIGIBLE(x, phi) := DOF(x) > 0 ∧ Coupled_AE(x) ∧ Declared(phi) ∧ OrderedIntermediate(x, phi) ∧ EndpointCompatible(x, phi) ∧ GenExclusionBeforeClosure(x, phi)

RateTypeFailure.definition: The recorded failure class returned when a rate-typed bridge candidate does not satisfy the declared eligibility conditions.

BridgeAdmissibilityScreen.definition: The governed screen that separates bridge admission from bridge testing and keeps admissibility distinct from promotion.

formal_reading.interpretation: The predicate is an admission screen, not a bridge proof, not a theorem, and not a modification of RT_core.

governance_rules.rule: No rate-based metric bridge may be evaluated until RATE_TYPE_ELIGIBLE(x, phi) is checked and its pass or failure class is recorded.
Passing RATE_TYPE_ELIGIBLE(x, phi) does not promote RATE_UNIFICATION_001, DENSITY_BRIDGE_001, or Non-Realizability of Decoupled Endpoints. It only admits the candidate to bridge testing.
Narrative expansion without a new predicate, invariant, or falsifiable consequence is not validation.

failure_modes.meaning: The system has zero degrees of freedom.
The A|E relation is not coupled.
The reference phi is not declared.
Evaluation is attempted only at the endpoints.
The endpoint relation is not compatible with the declared reference.
Generative exclusion before closure is missing.

forbidden_inferences: Passing RATE_TYPE_ELIGIBLE does not prove bridge truth.
Passing RATE_TYPE_ELIGIBLE does not promote DENSITY_BRIDGE_001.
Passing RATE_TYPE_ELIGIBLE does not promote RATE_UNIFICATION_001.
Passing RATE_TYPE_ELIGIBLE does not imply endpoint realizability.
Passing RATE_TYPE_ELIGIBLE does not modify RT_core.

Add the ordered trace that records the failure-first evaluation pipeline for RATE_TYPE_ELIGIBLE(x, phi).
Add the counterexample witness that blocks zero-DOF, decoupled, undeclared, endpoint-only, mismatch, and no-exclusion readings.
Add the governed rate-type eligibility clarification and lexicon debt entry for the new predicate.
Register RATE_TYPE_ELIGIBLE, propagation_position, and Non-Realizability of Decoupled Endpoints as GAP_OPEN terms.
Register the proposed rate-type eligibility execution-surface update in the governance ledger.
Register the new documentation surfaces, the patch record, and the updated textbook and ledger hashes.

textbook_integration.recommended_location: Section 2.8, immediately after Delta Ordinal Boundary Dynamics and before the field-candidate note.
textbook_integration.integration_note: Introduce RATE_TYPE_ELIGIBLE(x, phi) as the governance screen that must be checked before any rate-based metric-bridge evaluation. Passing the screen admits bridge testing only; it does not promote any bridge claim.

governance_notes: This patch adds an admissibility predicate, not a bridge promotion.
The predicate keeps failure classes explicit and records them before any bridge testing.
